images.filename: Lincoln's favorite horse on the day of his master's funeral, Lincoln Home National Historic Site, 1865. (46fd6d2b5db24fbb8f63ac905e214ea3).jpg
images.caption:
Lincoln loved his dog, Fido, and had an affinity for cats. He also loved horses. He had several during his life, including Tom, Belle, Old Buck and Robin - who was commonly nicknamed 'Old Bob'. When one of his horses went missing, Lincoln placed an ad in the Sangamo Journal pleading for his lost friend: "From a stable in Springfield, on Wednesday, 18th inst. a large bay horse, star in his forehead, plainly marked with harness; supposed to be eight years old; had been shod all round, but is believed to have lost some of his shoes, and trots and paces. Any person who will take up said horse, and leave information at the Journal office, or with the subscriber at New-Salem, shall be literally paid for their trouble. A. LINCOLN." Pictured: Old Bob on the day of his master's final funeral.

images.filename: President Abraham Lincoln's funeral train, Lincoln Home National Historic Site, 1865. (6128074fb49b4391b748376b38cb8c3f).jpg
images.caption:
President Lincoln's body would travel through 180 cities and seven states before reaching its final resting place a few weeks later. The funeral procession began April 21, 1865 on the Lincoln Special, the funeral train that would carry him to Springfield, Illinois for burial on May 4. Departing Washington's Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Depot, the train made stops in Baltimore and Harrisburg, Pennsylvania where a hearse then carried the coffin to the state House of Representatives where it was open for viewing later that night. Willie Lincoln's coffin was also aboard, on its way to be buried with his father.
Keywords: lincoln; president lincoln; mr lincoln; president; presidential; funeral train; funeral; death; abraham lincoln
